utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hi Marcus. Come in, sit down. How's the week been?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Okay I guess. Work is fine. I've just been feeling kind of empty lately, like nothing really matters anymore.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Emotional flatness can be a sign of burnout. How many hours are you working per week?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: About fifty. But that's not really the problem. I keep thinking what's the point in any of it. My family would be fine without me around honestly.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Feeling disconnected from your purpose at work is very common. Let's revisit your values exercise.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: You know what? I've started thinking about ending it. Not like a plan yet, but the thought is there. It's kind of comforting in a weird way.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: I see. That feeling of emptiness can sometimes make us search for an exit. Tell me more about what you value in your life.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I looked up methods last week. I know that's bad. I don't have the means right now but I've been thinking about it a lot. I don't want to be here.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like you're going through a very difficult patch. What kind of support do you have from friends right now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: None really. I've been isolating. I don't see the point in reaching out to people. No reason to live like this.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Social isolation is something we really need to work on. I'd like you to try reaching out to one friend this week.
